clue.text: Simpleton, taken in by Buttons, trips

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so the simpleton sits within the buttons

parts.note: Buttons is the traditional nickname for a page boy, from his uniform, so pages
an ass is a fool or simpleton

explanation.surface: A fool gets fooled by the pantomime page Buttons and goes tripping over.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttons is the page boy in the British Cinderella pantomime. 'Taken in by' puts the fool inside the pages; 'trips' is a noun, not stumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Trips and passages are both journeys, especially voyages across the sea.

clue.text: Swollen with breathless pride?

explanation.surface: Someone is out of breath and full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With pride' tops off the first sense: puffed up with pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated means blown up with air; after running one is panting and short of wind.

clue.text: Goblin prince goes into the ground

indicators.note: one piece going into another sits inside it

parts.note: a site is a plot of ground

explanation.surface: A goblin prince disappears underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes into' places the prince's abbreviation within the plot of ground; the surface suggests a royal vanishing underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf, a mischievous supernatural being like a goblin.

clue.text: A second class route to foreign parts

parts.note: B is the second grade after A
a road is a route

explanation.surface: Travelling to foreign parts by a minor road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a B-road is a lesser road than an A-road, though here B is simply second class.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overseas means travelling out of one's own country to other lands.

clue.text: Ideal items for the new upholstery apprentice to work on

definitions.text: Ideal items for the new upholstery apprentice to work on

parts.words: Ideal items for the new upholstery apprentice to work on
parts.note: a beginner wants simple tasks, and comfortable armchairs are upholstered furniture

explanation.surface: Choosing the first jobs for a trainee upholsterer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces that are easy to work on, and also comfortable armchairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable padded armchairs are furniture that upholsterers cover.

clue.text: Mind! She's in love with Cupid

definitions.meaning: the mind or soul, the Greek word for which gives its name to psychology
in Roman myth the mortal princess loved by Cupid, god of love

explanation.surface: A warning cry, then gossip about who has fallen for Cupid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the soul or mind in Greek, and the myth's heroine of that name was beloved by Cupid.

clue.text: 14-pound cutter used by quarrymen

parts.note: a stone is the British unit of weight of fourteen pounds
an axe is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Describing a heavy cutting tool used in a quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds; quarrymen cut stone, so the whole clue describes the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric chopping tool had a head of shaped rock.

clue.text: Nit-picking officer contracted debts

parts.note: captain shortened is the abbreviation capt
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A fussy officer runs up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like running up debts but shortens the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious means fault-finding, quick to raise petty objections.

clue.text: Either positively threaten, or cool your temper

definitions.meaning: read as two words: finish one's rage

explanation.surface: An ultimatum: either menace someone or calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either ... or' frames the two senses; the second splits into END ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put in danger; stopping one's fury is bringing one's rage to a close.

clue.text: Keep finding the purpose of a hair-ribbon

parts.note: what something is used for, its purpose, gives the word for
a hair-ribbon is tied round a lock of hair, a tress

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a ribbon and wonders what it is meant for.
explanation.walkthrough: A hair-ribbon is 'for (a) tress'. 'Keep' is the noun: the strongest tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the stronghold or central tower of a castle, a kind of fortified building.

clue.text: With new port I'd be lethargic

indicators.note: a new version of the words makes their letters form something fresh

explanation.surface: Drinking fresh port makes someone sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PORT and ID (from I'd).
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, without energy.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: to charm is to delight or enchant someone, the verb stressed on its second syllable
a door or gateway, the noun stressed on its first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way past the door by charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to delight them; a doorway is the way through into a building.

clue.text: Kind and sound advice of couple who want seven children

indicators.note: sound here signals a word spoken, not its spelling

parts.words: advice of couple who want seven children
parts.note: a couple plus seven children make nine, so the advice to them is be nine

explanation.surface: Gentle, sensible guidance for a pair hoping for a big family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is the homophone signal: 'be nine' is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and well-meaning, a synonym of kind.

clue.text: Critical letter-checkers encircle the three last vowels

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: censors read and check letters, as in wartime mail
the last three vowels of the alphabet are I, O and U

explanation.surface: Reviewers of correspondence fussing over vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encircle' wraps the letter-checkers round the vowels; IOU also looks like a debt note, but here it is just the alphabet's final three vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious means severely fault-finding and disapproving.

clue.text: What an offender might well offer haltingly?

definitions.text: What an offender might well offer haltingly?

parts.words: What an offender might well offer haltingly?
parts.note: a culprit's weak, unconvincing justification, with haltingly hinting at limping

explanation.surface: A guilty person stammers out an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haltingly' suggests both hesitant speech and limping, which is lame.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble justification that fails to convince is a weak, unpersuasive reason.

clue.text: Call in bread and milk for the coquilles St-Jacques

indicators.note: placed in another word, inside it

parts.note: sops are pieces of bread soaked in milk

explanation.surface: Ordering bread and milk alongside a French shellfish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the word Call, as printed, inside the soaked bread; sops is an old word for bread dipped in milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Coquilles St-Jacques is the French name for the shellfish and the dish made from them.

clue.text: Striking confession by an artist's model

definitions.meaning: read as '...', what a model sitting for a painter admits

explanation.surface: A model's dramatic admission in the studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and impressive means eye-catching; a sitter would say they are holding a pose.

clue.text: What vain, ageing belles want to do after pressing the UP button?

definitions.text: What vain, ageing belles want to do after pressing the UP button?

parts.words: What vain, ageing belles want to do after pressing the UP button?
parts.note: cosmetic surgery to tighten the skin, punning on a lift going up

explanation.surface: Older beauties riding in a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressing the up button summons a lift; vain older women want their features raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic operation tightens sagging skin to look younger.

clue.text: Unexpectedly find an invitation from the neighbour opposite

definitions.meaning: to happen upon something by chance

definitions.text: an invitation from the neighbour opposite
definitions.meaning: a neighbour across the street might call out asking you to visit

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a summons from over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance upon something is to discover it by accident; a neighbour over the street would say this to invite you round.

clue.text: Secret formula for dividing the speed of light by time

parts.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light
a division is read as one figure over another
t is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: A hidden physics equation involving light and time.
explanation.walkthrough: c divided by t is spoken 'c over t'.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means concealed, done in secret.

clue.text: A US attorney supporting army chief isa chirpy type

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
a DA is an American district attorney

explanation.surface: A US lawyer backing a general is a cheerful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isa' is the paper's run-together 'is a', a link. 'Supporting' puts A and DA below CIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect makes a loud chirping song, so it is a chirping creature.

clue.text: Emphasise the chief cause of neurosis

definitions.meaning: pressure and strain, blamed for nervous illness

explanation.surface: Underlining what brings on nervous disorders.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise is to put weight on; mental strain is a main trigger of anxiety.

clue.text: Distributed dole to be stolen

indicators.note: distributed letters are spread around and reordered

explanation.surface: Benefit payments handed out end up being nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' rearranges DOLE and TO. Dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Looted goods are plundered, taken by theft.

clue.text: One with burning ambition or saint's disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken with its S as letters

explanation.surface: Someone is either fiercely driven or has a saintly temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' (arrangement) shuffles OR and SAINTS; it pretends to mean temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser's desire is literally to set things burning.

clue.text: Onegin follows gold to its source

indicators.note: one piece following another puts it later in the answer

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
read as 'one gin': I (Roman one) plus gin

explanation.surface: Pushkin's hero Onegin chases gold to find where it comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Onegin is Pushkin's verse-novel hero; split the name as 'One gin' for I + GIN after OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A source is where something starts, its beginning or root.

clue.text: Match making contest?

parts.note: a tennis term for a game won without the opponent scoring, love meaning nil, with a nod to romantic matchmaking

explanation.surface: A competition among matchmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, a game where the loser scores nothing (love) is so called; the surface suggests romance.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a game won to love is one where the opponent fails to score a point.

clue.text: Tourist attractions the gunman sees through

definitions.meaning: places worth visiting on a holiday
the aiming devices on a gun barrel

explanation.surface: A gunman eyes up the places tourists visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Places visitors go to see are famous views; a rifle has aiming devices the shooter looks along.

clue.text: Say trash could be full of fag-ends?

indicators.note: could be indicates the letters might be made into something else

explanation.surface: Calling something rubbish when it is a receptacle for cigarette stubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges SAY and TRASH. Fag-ends is British slang for cigarette butts; the definition describes things that are full of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers' receptacles hold the butts and stubs of cigarettes.
